note: Found on 2026-10-03 in review, by a random run of 40 inversions. A Schlumberger sounding from 3 m that reads 40 ohm-m at the first spacing and about 6 ohm-m from 5 m out. Both engines converge to two layers at the same misfit (7.817 percent, equal to 1e-3), with a top layer of 920 ohm-m and 0.702 m in Python and 939 ohm-m and 0.699 m in the browser. The Python inversion rates the boundary resolved (thickness uncertain by a factor of 1.07), so the comparison's carve-out for poorly resolved models does not apply; what the data do not fix is the top layer's resistivity, which that factor does not measure. A top layer a quarter of the first spacing thick is seen only through the product of its resistivity and thickness, and each search stopped at a different point along it.
open: The same question as ves-equivalent-models.json, for a resistivity: should parity hold the two engines to 1e-3 on a layer parameter the data do not determine, and should the resolution the toolkit reports (today the thickness factor only) cover resistivities too, so that such a layer is said to be unresolved and left out of the comparison as a poorly resolved boundary is? Until that is decided the nightly run will draw cases of this kind; this one is held to diverging.
